data.body:
LANDED. Gerrit change 1615 merged at 06:09 UTC as commit 22602d81bd on origin/main (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments). All 22 CI jobs green on run 31567345223, including all four pytest cells and all 7 mutation shards.

All 11 acceptance criteria verified against the MERGED tree:
- AC1/AC4: 2 occurrences of --timeout=900 --timeout-method=thread in external-integration.yml (llm_live matrix + Jira DC harness)
- AC2: 1 x --timeout=600 (live Jira Cloud)
- AC3: 1 x --timeout=300 (Langfuse trace)
- AC5: 1 x --timeout=3600 (structured-output sweep)
- AC6: 1 x --timeout=600 (test.yml external tier)
- AC7: 300s on both offline lanes, and _optionality's clean venv installs pytest-timeout
- AC8/AC8b: parity suite 17 passed on the landed tree; the four-invocation-form flag-removal experiments were run before landing and each produced a failure
- AC9: every per-lane budget carries its evidence as a YAML comment at the step it governs
- AC10: make lint (incl. actionlint over all workflows) and make typecheck green; no lane's selection, markers or behavior changed beyond the added flags

Notes for the record. The landing took three patchsets, and none of the delays were defects in this work: (1) the known s3_doctor bad-object flake (wrongful-chemic-squeaker, now with its third recorded occurrence); (2) two mutation-gate timeouts that were a gate-rollout artifact - the runs executed the OLD serial walking-skeleton workflow because reusable workflows resolve at main's ref, not the patchset, and a rebase cleared it. I filed frowsy-beggarly-mammoth during that second episode and both of my hypotheses on it were subsequently refuted; the ticket has been corrected and the error owned there. No --timeout added by this change ever fired in CI.

Closing: the class is now fully guarded. All eight pytest lanes in .github/workflows carry a per-test hang guard, and the extended parity sweep fails if any future lane ships without one.
